children: AutoNation
delivered a mixed third quarter as weaker new- and used-vehicle sales pressured the core dealership business, while stronger after-sales and finance operations helped support earnings.
Third-quarter revenue came in at about
$7.01 billion
, roughly flat from $7.04 billion a year earlier. Seeking Alpha reported the figure ahead of expectations, though other consensus providers showed slightly different estimates.
Adjusted EPS rose
2% year over year to $5.11
, marking AutoNation's seventh consecutive quarter of adjusted EPS growth. GAAP EPS, however, fell to $4.87 from $5.65.
The core vehicle business remained under pressure.
New-vehicle revenue fell to about
$3.33 billion from $3.42 billion
, while same-store new-vehicle retail unit sales declined 6% through the first nine months of the year. Same-store used-vehicle unit sales also fell 6%.
But AutoNation's higher-margin businesses helped offset some of that weakness.
Parts and service revenue increased to about
$1.29 billion from $1.23 billion
, while the company reported record after-sales gross profit and 6% growth in customer-pay service.
AutoNation Finance is also becoming a more meaningful contributor.
Its portfolio grew more than
40% year over year
, while profit increased roughly tenfold.
Capital returns provided another boost.
AutoNation repurchased about
$620 million of stock year to date
, reducing shares outstanding by roughly 9%, and the board authorized another
$1 billion in buybacks
Investor Takeaway
I think the key story is that AutoNation is becoming
less dependent on selling more cars to grow per-share earnings
Vehicle volumes are soft.
But service, parts, finance, and buybacks are doing more of the heavy lifting.
That matters because dealership margins can compress quickly when unit demand weakens, while after-sales and finance tend to be more recurring and higher margin.
The risk is that those businesses may not fully offset prolonged weakness in new- and used-car sales.
For investors, the key things to watch are
vehicle unit trends, gross profit per vehicle, after-sales growth, AutoNation Finance profitability, and the pace of share repurchases
AutoNation's dealership volumes are under pressure.
Its earnings model is becoming more diversified.

title: AutoNation's Strong Quarter Comes With a Sales Warning
